India and Poland today agreed to strengthen cooperation in areas of defence, space and
nuclear energy.
Both countries decided to establish a defence industry dialogue, an institute of formal
dialogue and counter-terrorism.
The two countries also set the target of doubling bilateral trade by 2030.
The major announcements were made following comprehensive talks between Prime Minister
Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart, Donald Tusk, in New Delhi.
The two leaders discussed bilateral, regional and global issues of mutual interest, addressing
a joint press briefing after the meeting, Prime Minister Modi invited Polish companies
to engage with India in the co-development and co-production of technologies in strategic
sectors of defence, space and nuclear energy.

Welcome back to the news at 9.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu today exchanged
views on recent developments in West Asia and stressed the urgent need to restore
peace and stability in the region.
Mr. Modi received a telephone call from the Prime Minister of Israel.
During their conversation, Prime Minister Modi reiterated India's call for dialogue
and diplomacy as the way forward.
They reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the special strategic
partnership between the two countries.
India has condemned the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructures in
Saudi Arabia.
These include the attack on King Fahad International Airport in Dhammam and Saudi's Aramco
Sheba oil field in the eastern province yesterday which resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.
The external affairs ministry in a statement reiterated that the attacks on civilian critical
infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must seize immediately.
The ministry informed that one Indian national died and two others were injured in the
attack on Dhamma map while another Indian national was injured in the attack on the
Sheba oil field.
Meanwhile, the government has stepped up efforts to facilitate the early return of
affected Indian Umrah pilgrims from Saudi Arabia. The minister said in a statement that
the Indian embassy in Riyadh and the consulate in Jeddah are actively coordinating with airlines
and tour operators to help them return home at the earliest. It said over the past week
about 3,000 stranded Umrah pilgrims have returned to India from Saudi Arabia on available
flights. This is in addition to more than 10,000 normal Umrah pilgrims who were booked
on the available flights and have traveled back to India over the past week. 24 by
seven control rooms have been established to help
Indian nationals and regular advisories are being issued. The contact details of the control
rooms at Embassy of India and Riyadh are plus 96654412016, 96542126784. The toll-free
number for calls within Saudi Arabia is 8002471234 and the WhatsApp number for messages
messages only is 966536216082. The contact details of the 24x7 control rooms at Consulate
General in Jedha are 966122614093 and 966616122301. The WhatsApp number for messages only is
966-536-209-704. Our correspondent has filed this report.
Airports at Jeddah, Medina and Damam remain operational, although some flight disruptions
continue. Indian carriers have extended the suspension of their services to and from Saudi Arabia.
Air India, Air India Express and Indigo have suspended their services till 24th October.
Akasa Air has suspended its flights until 27th of this month. However, alternative flight options
remain available through other airlines including Saudi and flying-ass.
Meanwhile, Indian nationals have been advised to verify flight arrangements before travelling,
follow the guidelines of local Saudi authorities, and continue to observe the safety precautions
outlined in the advisories issued by the Embassy of India in Riyadh.
Supranasekhyam, Agashwani News, Delhi.
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan today launched the nationwide
Kheth Bachao Abhyan Rabi 2026 from Karnal in Haryana.
The campaign will continue till the 30th of next month.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Chauhan said, the center's top priority is to protect
the dignity, honor, and self-respect of farmers and the farming profession.
Today the Kheth Bachao Abhyan is being launched across the country.
The land is our mother, the food grains, fruits and vegetables that we eat are grown in this
very soil.
However, the excessive and imbalanced uses of fertilizer and pesticides is deteriorating
the health of our mother earth.
It is in everyone's interest that we use fertilizer and pesticides in a balanced manner.
And balanced use means using only as much as necessary.
President Rob De Moomoo today attended the Seva Samman Parva and Yuva Prabodhan events
at Rai Purin Chhattisgarh's part of the celebrations marking Nua Khai, a major harvest festival.
Addressing the gathering, the President said the event is a reflection of the region's
rich traditions, social harmony and unity.
And, in the coming centuries, India will have the opportunity to reach the living world.
At the Asian Paragames, Indian contingent continued its impressive performance at Aichi Nagoya
in Japan, taking the country's overall medals tally past the 80 mark.
The country bagged 26 medals including 7 gold, 4 silver and 15 bronze on the 4th day today.
With this, India's overall tally has risen to 88 including 21 gold, 26 silver and 41
bronze medals.
India is currently placed fourth in the overall standings.
Armless archer Sheetal Devi reigned supreme in the women's compound individual and mixed
team events to claim gold in both the competitions.
Sheetal along with Toman Kumar backed gold in the compound mixed team event.
In men's cricket India defeated host New Zealand by four wickets in the first T20
international at Christchurch today to take a 1-0 lead in the five-man series, chasing
a target of 226 runs.
India scored 2-30 for 6 in 19.4 overs to seal victory with two balls to spare.
Earlier, put into bat, New Zealand posted an imposing total of 225 for four in the
stipulated 20 overs.
The benchmark domestic equity indices ended lower today, extending their losses for the
third consecutive session.
The sensex dropped 460 points to close at 73,249.
The NIFTY declined 124 points to settle at 22,688.
The India Meteorological Department has issued orange color warning for heavy to
very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Purcheri and Karaykal tomorrow.
for Delhi, the weather agency has forecast a clear sky tomorrow.
